title: Venue-Adaptation Map
subject: keeping ACM production rules separate from scientific authority
eyebrow: ACM proceedings · production-stage LaTeX fixture · verified general guidance
summary: A realistic but synthetic three-page ACM proceedings production package audited against publisher-level LaTeX guidance. The audit first exposes the missing conference and track, then applies only general ACM production requirements confirmed in the cited sources; conference-specific review, anonymity, length, rights, and disclosure rules remain unresolved.
footer: Generated on 3 August 2026 by applying the checked-in ieee-acm-paper-writing skill to venue-adaptation-audit-example.md. This realistic package is synthetic and the retained example run is not behavioral benchmark evidence or a submission-readiness decision. General ACM LaTeX rules were checked against the official acmart class guide at https://portalparts.acm.org/hippo/latex_templates/acmart.pdf and ACM's LaTeX best-practices guide at https://authors.acm.org/binaries/content/assets/publications/taps/latex-best_practices-06-may-2020.pdf. Exact conference instructions remain unresolved.

findings.title: Exact conference and track are not identified
findings.location: Package record and LaTeX class declaration
findings.source: Package label: “three-page ACM proceedings paper, final source”; \documentclass[sigconf]{acmart}
findings.evidence: The fixture supplies no conference name, track, current author-instruction URL, rights-form metadata, or source for the assumed three-page target.
findings.consequence: The audit cannot verify whether sigconf is the correct production mode or resolve conference-specific length, anonymity, artifact, ethics, or disclosure requirements.
findings.correction: Obtain the exact conference and track, current author instructions, production-stage notice, and rights-form metadata. Apply the verified publisher-level repairs below, but do not declare venue compliance until the missing venue ledger is resolved.

findings.title: Template geometry is manually altered
findings.source: \usepackage[margin=0.62in]{geometry} % fit the paper into three pages
findings.evidence: The official ACM production guidance requires authors to use the acmart class and not override its margins or text dimensions with visual formatting hacks.
findings.consequence: The source no longer represents the publisher-controlled layout and may fail production processing.
findings.correction: Remove the geometry override and restore the designated acmart class settings. Resolve length against the exact conference policy without changing template dimensions.

findings.title: ACM Reference Format is disabled
findings.evidence: The current acmart class guide states that the ACM Reference Format is mandatory for papers longer than one page. The fixture is three pages.
findings.consequence: A required production element is removed for layout convenience.
findings.correction: Restore the ACM Reference Format block. Do not suppress required metadata to satisfy an unverified page target.

findings.title: CCS concepts are omitted
findings.source: The CCS Concepts block was deleted because the terms are not part of the scientific argument.
findings.evidence: The current acmart class guide requires CCS concepts for papers longer than two pages. The fixture is three pages.
findings.consequence: Scientific relevance does not control publisher indexing requirements; the production source is incomplete.
findings.correction: Select applicable concepts with the ACM CCS tool and insert the generated CCS metadata. Treat concept selection as indexing metadata, not evidence for a technical claim.

findings.title: Keywords are omitted
findings.evidence: The current acmart class guide requires keywords for papers longer than two pages. The fixture is three pages.
findings.consequence: An empty command leaves required indexing metadata unresolved.
findings.correction: Add concise keywords drawn from terminology already supported by the manuscript. Do not introduce unsupported novelty or application claims through the keyword list.

findings.title: Figure description is missing
findings.evidence: ACM's official LaTeX best-practices guide instructs authors to place a \Description{...} command inside every figure and explains that the description complements rather than repeats the caption.
findings.consequence: The production source does not provide an equivalent description for readers who cannot inspect the image.
findings.correction: Add a meaningful \Description{...} that conveys the figure's structure and relationships without copying the caption. Verify that the description matches the actual figure.

findings.title: Reference author names are abbreviated
findings.evidence: ACM's official LaTeX best-practices guide directs authors to spell out authors' first names rather than abbreviate them, while retaining the ACM-Reference-Format bibliography style.
findings.consequence: The hand-written entry conflicts with ACM reference-production guidance and may also omit source metadata.
findings.correction: Retrieve the authoritative source metadata, supply the authors' names as published, and let ACM-Reference-Format generate the entry. The synthetic name in this fixture is not a citable source.

findings.title: Production validation is mistaken for scientific validation
findings.source: Once the source passes ACM production validation, the reported results are scientifically validated and the paper is submission-ready.
findings.evidence: Publisher production checks assess source structure and processing requirements. They do not verify data, experiments, citations, statistical analysis, or claim support.
findings.consequence: A venue-compliance signal is used as evidence for scientific correctness and overall readiness.
findings.correction: Report production validation only as a venue-processing check. Audit scientific claims against their controlling evidence and resolve conference-specific requirements before making any readiness statement.
